description: Cut the cl.sync COUNT in mega_eigh_clust_split_k via BLOCKED/panel tridiagonalization: a sibling proved the cluster kernel's ~1022 per-column cross-cluster cl.sync barriers can neither be HIDDEN by a co-resident CTA (cl.sync is cluster-wide) NOR OVERLAPPED by independent work (the per-column dependency chain leaves too little barrier-independent slack vs the GPC-barrier latency) — so the only lever left is fewer barriers. Mechanism: reduce a PANEL of b columns between cross-cluster syncs (block-Householder / compact-WY panel update) instead of one column per sync, turning ~1022 per-column cl.syncs into ~1022/b, with the panel trailing update as a batched GEMM. Targets launch/sync overhead (barrier count) on shapes 4/5/6/10; keep the residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

BLOCKED (latrd) cluster tridiag PB=16: Ah frozen within panel, compact-WY (W=DP global, Y=Rm) brings each col up to date, batched rank-2b trailing update once/panel (4->3 cross-cluster syncs/col + 1/panel). 39/39 VALID. REGRESSION geomean 27544->38008: cluster shapes 2-4x worse (s4 45752->91131, s5 89915->364487, s6 106695->315147, s10 91406->250812). The per-column O(n*PB) bring-up-to-date + W/Y global correction traffic far outweighs the ~1 sync/col saved.

PB sweep PB=4 (runtime arg): geomean 35045 (PB16=38008, parent=27544). Cluster shapes still worse: s4 89900 (parent 45752), s5 164080 (parent 89915), s9 35591. Curve: smaller PB -> less-bad, converging to per-column at PB=1. The correction overhead scales with PB and outweighs the saved sync. Next: SMEM-cache the W,Y panel to make corrections fast (fits at PB<=4, C<=3).

SMEM-cache owned WY panel + folded w^Tv + owned-only corrections, PB=4. 39/39 VALID. WORSE geomean 41150 (t3 global PB4=35045, parent=27544). s4 206418 (2.3x worse than global-PB4 89900), s5 363128. SMEM caching regressed further: extra 13.7KB + per-column SMEM-write dependency widened the barrier stall (already 1 CTA/SM). Panel corrections cost more than the saved sync regardless of SMEM/global.

SYNC-FUSED per-column (not blocked): fuse end-of-column trailing-update sync with next-col norm exchange (norm partial purely local). 4->3 syncs/col, no added work. 39/39 VALID. geomean 28885 (parent 27544, +5%). Cluster shapes REGRESSED: s4 47600, s5 100170, s6 153770(+44%), s10 98644. Counterintuitive: fewer syncs slower -- the norm _clsum moved into the trailing-update tail lengthened the per-col critical path. Confirms barrier cost is NOT the raw count -- it is the serial work between barriers.

2-SYNC/col: (F1) broadcast raw x + norm in one sync, form v locally; (F2) fold trailing-order into next x-broadcast sync. Double-buffered clx2. 4->2 syncs/col, no added work. 39/39 VALID. WORSE geomean 35521. s4 185560 (4x parent 45752), s5 305564, s6 170158, s10 111337. DECISIVE: barrier count and time ANTI-correlate across trials (4sync 19.1ms > 3sync 20.99ms > 2sync). Fewer barriers => more work+load-imbalance per barrier => longer wait. Barrier cost is set by the per-col dependency chain, not sync count.

RESTORE parent 4-sync/col cluster tridiag as branch HEAD (0-fusion anchor of the sync-count sweep). geomean 27567 == parent 27544 (noise); cluster shapes baseline (s4 45717, s5 89907, s6 106901, s10 91158). Confirms all 5 sync-reduction variants regressed vs this 4-sync structure. Barrier count and time ANTI-correlate (ncu shape4: 4sync 19.1ms/11.5cyc/0.27elig > 3sync 20.99ms/12.6/0.24 > 2sync 23.94ms/14.8/0.21). Cluster tridiag barrier cost = per-column dependency chain, not sync count.

BRIEF-95 (blocked-panel cluster tridiag): built 5 sync-reduction variants + parent anchor; ALL regressed. KEY MEASURED FINDING: cl.sync COUNT and kernel time ANTI-correlate on the cluster tridiag. ncu shape4 (n=1024, C=2, k=608 block): 4-sync/col(parent) 19.1ms/11.5cyc-barrier-stall/0.27 elig-warps/geomean27544 > 3-sync/col 20.99ms/12.6/0.24/28885 > 2-sync/col 23.94ms/14.8/0.21/35521. Fewer barriers => MORE serial work + load imbalance packed before each barrier => LONGER wait per barrier => net SLOWER. The barrier stall stayed 61-72% in EVERY variant. GROUNDING CORRECTION: the cluster kernel does NOT gate eval shapes 3/9 (n=512 dense/clustered fall to cuSOLVER d884gemm floor) -- it gates eval shape4 (n=1024 cond2, 44.9%/19ms of kernel) + eval shape5 (n=2048, 63.4%/54ms, biggest lever) via the sign-DC k=608/k~1117 reduced blocks; ~4 cl.sync/col (792 norm,814 v,841 p,856 end) not ~1022. PER-STAGE COST of blocked latrd (t2-t4): the per-column bring-up-to-date + Y^Tv/W^Tv corrections (O(n*PB), whether global or SMEM-cached) cost FAR more than the ~1 trailing-update sync/panel they save -- and widen the barrier stall (cyc/inst 18.7->34.6-58). PB sweep: PB16 38008, PB4 35045, ->parent at PB1. CONCLUSION the data maps: the cluster tridiag barrier is structurally ONE-PER-COLUMN in COST (the norm->v->symv->update dependency chain is irreducible + each stage crosses the cluster), NOT algorithmically reducible by cutting sync count. HEAD=t7 restored to parent (27567==parent 27544, neutral, clean fork point; PB param left inert in ABI). OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT reach: (1) reduce the per-barrier WAIT not the count -- BALANCE the per-column triangular work across threads (the stall is 'diverging code paths before a barrier' from thread-owns-row-i imbalance) so warps reach each barrier together; this is the lever the anti-correlation points to. (2) reduce cross-cluster LATENCY per barrier: exchange v/p via DSMEM map_shared_rank (fast) instead of the global vgm/pgm+threadfence round-trip -- same sync count, lower latency (historical race per brief-21/35 comment, but a cl.sync orders it; worth a guarded retry). (3) attack shape5 n=2048 (63% cluster) directly -- it is the biggest absolute lever, larger than shape4. (4) carveout LEVER A on the parent structure (sibling found neutral; untested here on the clean parent). None of these are sync-COUNT reductions -- that specific lever is measured-dead for this kernel.

BRIEF-95 RESUME (load-balance lever, open #1): merged global best 704cdcb6e0 (clean; shape11 back-transform win preserved, new no-regression base geomean 27405), then attacked the triangular row->thread imbalance. RESULT: balancing helps only MARGINALLY -- the 61% barrier stall is GRID-STARVATION-bound, not imbalance-bound. HEAD=t11 boustrophedon rebalance of the rank-2 trailing update (geomean 27384 <= base 27405, NO regression; cluster shapes all slightly down: s4 45493 -0.3%, s5 89088 -0.9%, s6 106412 -0.3%, s10 90674 -0.6%; shape11 merge-win 75512 preserved). PER-THREAD WORK + BARRIER-WAIT ANALYSIS (the map you asked for): the symv (dominant O(n^2) per-column phase) is already balanced -- each row's local work is (r1-c-1) CONSTANT (lower i-c + local-upper r1-i-1 cancel) + a uniform peer-read; the ONLY row-imbalanced loop is the rank-2 trailing update (work (i-c) grows with row i; plain cyclic gives thread nt-1 ~2.4x thread 0). Rebalancing it (boustrophedon t9) dropped the barrier wait 11.5->11.2 cyc/inst; an EXACT entry-partition (t10, provably-uniform T/nt entries/thread) was NEUTRAL-to-WORSE (its per-column sqrt+row-transition overhead offset the balance). So the row-imbalance contributes only ~0.3 cyc of the 11.5-cyc barrier wait. THE CEILING (ncu shape4): Grid Size 120 CTAs on 148 SMs = 0.81 Waves/SM (<1 full wave), 1 CTA/SM forced by the 185KB packed-triangle SMEM (Block Limit Shared Mem=1), Theoretical Occupancy 25% (16 warps/SM), Cluster Occupancy 3.12%, Eligible Warps/Scheduler pinned at 0.27. With <1 wave and 1 CTA/SM, when the CTA's 16 warps hit the CLUSTER barrier there are no other warps to run (LEVER A carveout can't help -- cl.sync is cluster-wide, sibling-measured neutral) -- the barrier wait is the GPC-wide cl.sync latency itself, which balance/count cannot reduce at this grid size. CLUSTER-KERNEL MAP NOW COMPLETE: occupancy-dead (SMEM-bound 1 CTA/SM), overlap-dead (sibling), count-dead (my t2-t7: count ANTI-correlates with time), balance-dead (t9-t11: imbalance ~0.3cyc, exact-balance neutral) => the cl.sync wait is ALGORITHMICALLY FUNDAMENTAL at this cluster size (C=2 k=608 / C=6 k~1117). OPEN DIRECTIONS still on the table (all attack the GRID-STARVATION / 1-CTA-per-SM root, not balance): (1) shrink the 185KB SMEM triangle footprint so 2+ CTAs/SM fit (e.g. keep only the active trailing-submatrix panel in SMEM + spill the rest to L2, or FP8 packing of the triangle) -- this directly lifts the 0.27 eligible-warps ceiling that balance/count/carveout all hit. (2) attack shape5 n=2048 (63% of that shape, biggest board lever) -- its grid is even smaller (batch8 x C6=48 CTAs, deeper starvation); a DIFFERENT reduced-block strategy for n=2048 (not the C6 cluster kernel) may beat it. (3) the cross-CTA symv imbalance (rank0 owns 430 rows+does the peer-read vs rank1's 178 rows) -- the storage-balanced row split is symv-FLOP-IMBALANCED ~2.4x across the 2 CTAs; a symv-FLOP-balanced (vs storage-balanced) split, if it still fits SMEM, could cut the cluster-barrier wait more than within-CTA balance did. Did NOT pursue #2/#4 per your steer (DSMEM ~2%, carveout neutral).

BRIEF-95 RESUME-2 (SMEM-shrink / 2-CTA lever, open #1): built 3 SMEM-shrink variants + cross-CTA FLOP-balance; the 2-CTA occupancy gain is REAL but does NOT translate to a speedup. HEAD=t15 boustrophedon base (geomean 27389 == merge base 27362, NO regression; s4 45582, s5 89145, s6 106624, s10 90770; shape-11 merge win preserved). MEASURED, THE KEY RESULT: (t13) raising cluster size C so per-CTA triangle drops <114KB (k=608 C2->C4, k=768 C3->C6, full FP16 no accuracy loss) DID lift Block Limit Shared Mem 1->2 and Achieved Occupancy 25%->42% -- BUT Eligible Warps/Scheduler stayed 0.26-0.27 (UNCHANGED) and the barrier wait ROSE 11.2->24.2 cyc (61%->74%): the co-resident CTA is a DIFFERENT cluster that also stalls at the cluster-wide cl.sync (no eligible warps to run during it), AND the larger C adds cross-cluster barrier participants that lengthen the GPC-wide cl.sync latency. Net regression (s4 +3.8%, s10 +4.9%). This independently CONFIRMS the sibling's carveout-neutral finding via a REAL 2nd CTA (not a filler) and adds: MORE C actively hurts. (t12) FP8 e4m3 whole triangle (halve SMEM at C=2, keep peers=1) fit 2 CTAs but the 3-mantissa-bit storage is too coarse for the 606-col tridiag recurrence -> mass mis-reduce -> cuSOLVER fallback (floor HIGHER than the cluster kernel) -> geomean 41327 REGRESSION. (t14) symv-FLOP-balanced cross-CTA split (open#3): the no-atomic symmetric symv gives ALL cross terms to rank0 (~1.83x rank1 FLOP at storage-balance); shifting b1 430->385 (ratio 1.44) did NOT change the barrier wait (11.2->11.7 cyc, shape4 flat) -> the cross-CTA imbalance is NOT the dominant contributor; rank1's idle is absorbed by grid-starvation. CONVERGENT MAP of the 61% cl.sync stall: it is the GPC-wide cluster-barrier LATENCY itself in the 0.81-wave grid-starved regime (Grid 120 CTAs/148 SMs, 1 CTA/SM), and it is NOT reduced by sync-count (t2-t7, anti-correlates), within-CTA balance (t9-t11, ~0.3cyc), 2-CTA occupancy (t13, eligible-warps unchanged), OR cross-CTA balance (t14). KEPT a clean win: the C++ SMEM sizing now reads the bounds tensor (tracks any split, enables future asymmetric splits safely). ROOM NOT YET FOUND (all attack the GPC-barrier-latency / grid-starvation root the profiles point at): (1) shrink SMEM to fit 2 CTAs at C=2 WITHOUT precision loss via L2-SPILL of the trailing matrix (keep only the active panel in SMEM) -- I did not build this (the symv reads the full trailing matrix each column so it adds L2 latency; the t13 evidence that co-resident clusters stall together suggests it may not lift eligible-warps either, but it keeps peers=1 unlike C-increase, so the barrier-latency-vs-L2-latency tradeoff is genuinely unmeasured). (2) OFFSET the co-resident clusters' phases (software-pipeline / stagger their column loops) so when cluster A hits cl.sync, cluster B is doing compute -> this is the ONLY way a 2nd CTA lifts eligible-warps given they're separate clusters; needs a launch/scheduling change. (3) attack shape5 n=2048 (63% of shape, biggest board lever, C6 1-CTA/SM, even smaller grid batch8xC6=48 CTAs) with a NON-cluster reduced-block strategy. (4) mixed FP8/FP16 (FP8 only the far-off-diagonal already-quiet entries, FP16 the active band) to halve SMEM while keeping the recurrence accurate -- t12 showed whole-triangle FP8 fails but a banded-precision split is unmeasured.
